artworks.title: Prometheus Brings Fire to Mankind
artworks.description: Füger's torchbearer — the Titan carrying stolen fire down to humankind, the gift that names the myth and costs him the rock.

artworks.title: Prometheus Bound
artworks.description: Rubens' Philadelphia Bound — eagle and chains after the theft, Snyders' bird tearing the liver Hesiod and Aeschylus fixed as the price of fire.

artworks.title: Prometheus
artworks.description: Gilded bronze sculpture by Paul Manship overlooking the sunken plaza of Rockefeller Center in New York. Prometheus glides through a ring bearing the signs of the zodiac as he carries the stolen fire down to mankind, making him one of the most recognizable public artworks in America.

popCulture.title: Prometheus Bound
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus' (or his school's) rock-chained Titan — the fire-theft's aftermath as tragic defiance against Zeus.

popCulture.title: Prometheus
popCulture.description: The fire-theft remains modernity's favourite Titan myth — enlightenment, punishment, and the benefactor chained for humankind.

popCulture.title: Prometheus Unbound
popCulture.creator: Percy Bysshe Shelley
popCulture.description: Shelley's lyrical drama frees the fire-bringer — Romantic liberation rewriting Aeschylus' chained Titan as revolutionary hope.
